item.title: Full list: African countries where travelers can access without visa
item.description: Travelling across Africa is becoming easier as more countries adopt visa-free entry policies aimed at promoting tourism, strengthening regional integration and encouraging trade among African nations. Several African countries have introduced policies allowing citizens of other African countries to visit without obtaining a visa before travelling, reducing the cost and administrative hurdles associated with cross-border movement. Among the countries offering such access are Benin, The Gambia, Rwanda, Seychelles, Ghana and Togo. The policies form part of wider efforts to improve freedom of movement across the continent and advance the African Union’s goal of greater economic integration. The six countries are highlighted below, although their entry arrangements are not identical. 1. Benin Benin is one of Africa’s leading supporters of visa-free movement. It allows citizens of other African countries to enter without obtaining a visa before travelling. The country has promoted easier cross-border movement to encourage tourism, business and regional cooperation. 2. The Gambia The Gambia offers visa-free entry to citizens of other African countries. It is one of the continent’s more open destinations, making it attractive to visitors interested in tourism, business and cultural exchanges. 3. Rwanda Rwanda allows citizens of African Union member states to enter without a visa. The policy supports the country’s efforts to attract African visitors, investors and business travellers. 4. Seychelles Seychelles operates a visa-free entry policy for visitors of all nationalities, including African travellers. However, visitors must obtain the required travel authorisation before departure and meet the country’s entry conditions. 5. Ghana Ghana introduced a free visa policy for African nationals in May 2026. Under the arrangement, African travellers can apply for electronic visas without paying visa fees. However, an application and approval are still required, meaning the policy is not strictly visa-free entry. 6. Togo Togo has introduced visa-free entry for African passport holders, subject to pre-arrival requirements. The policy is part of efforts to facilitate movement across the continent and strengthen regional integration. item.title: Kano govt to Kwankwaso: Stop dragging Yusuf into EFCC troubles
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government has asked former Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso to stop linking Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf to his alleged dealings with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). The government said Yusuf had no involvement in Kwankwaso’s issues with the anti-graft agency, which it claimed predated the current administration. The Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, stated this in a statement issued on Friday. He described Kwankwaso’s allegations against the governor as misleading and politically motivated. According to the government, it was wrong for the former governor to accuse Yusuf of influencing the EFCC investigation when the matter began before his administration. “The crisis and court cases involving the NDC are internal party matters arising from disagreements among its members, and the Kano State Government has no involvement in them,” the statement said. The government accused Kwankwaso of using the governor as a target to gain public sympathy and remain politically relevant ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Rather than constantly blaming the Kano State Government for his political difficulties, Kwankwaso should concentrate on resolving the internal challenges confronting his political camp,” the statement said. It maintained that Yusuf was elected to govern Kano State and deliver development, not to engage in political arguments or take responsibility for the problems of other political parties. The government urged Kwankwaso to allow the administration to focus on fulfilling its promises to the people, warning that attempts to gain public sympathy through political blackmail would not succeed. “You cannot win public sympathy through blackmail and unfounded allegations,” it said. The statement added that the people of Kano State would have the opportunity to judge political leaders through their votes in 2027. It further reaffirmed that Yusuf remained committed to governance, development and the welfare of residents. Recall that Kwankwaso had accused Governor Yusuf of using the EFCC and other government institutions to target him and members of his family for political reasons ahead of the 2027 elections. He also alleged that the governor attempted to pressure the EFCC through protests at its office and interfere in a case involving the NDC governorship candidate. item.title: 2027: ‘Embrace Senator Orji Kalu’s adoption as consensus candidate’, Cleric tells Abia North aspirants

The cleric urged other aspirants seeking to represent Abia North in the Senate to accept the adoption of the former governor in good faith, congratulate him and join hands with other stakeholders in advancing the collective interests of the senatorial district. item.title: Fashola says election riggers deserve jail, not death
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has said people who manipulate election results should face imprisonment rather than execution, urging Nigerians to reject violent rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. Fashola made the remarks during a television interview on Friday while reacting to the “rig and die” statement attributed to Ovie Omo-Agege, a Delta Central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress. The former Minister of Works and Housing said electoral offences must be punished under the law, arguing that even where an offence attracts capital punishment, the accused must first be charged, tried and given an opportunity to defend themselves. “Absolutely not. I mean, come on. I think we must move away from what I think are extreme narratives and rhetoric,” Fashola said when asked whether election riggers should be killed. He stressed that the Electoral Act does not prescribe death as punishment for election rigging. “The punishment under the Electoral Act is not death. And even if it were death, which I will not support, there’s a process before you take human life; a charge, a trial, an opportunity to defend yourself,” he said. Fashola, however, maintained that election manipulation should attract serious punishment and urged politicians to seek votes through legitimate campaigns. “The penalty for rigging is not death. But don’t rig. Go and campaign for your party,” he added. He advised political parties to concentrate on mobilising voters in areas where they enjoy support rather than attempting to manipulate results in places where they have little electoral influence. The former governor also advocated stiffer prison sentences for serious electoral offences, suggesting that some violations should carry custodial penalties without the option of a fine. “I think maybe there might be stiffer sentences without the option of a fine, maybe a defined custodial sentence that is deterrent in nature,” he said. Fashola further called for greater public education on electoral conduct, noting that Nigeria had repeatedly amended its electoral laws without giving sufficient attention to educating citizens about the principles of democracy. He said sustained nationwide enlightenment would help reduce desperation during elections and encourage politicians and voters to understand that electoral contests could produce either winners or losers. item.description: Paris Fury, the wife of British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury, has withdrawn her earlier claim that her husband was diagnosed with schizophrenia, clarifying that he has never been formally diagnosed with the condition. Paris made the clarification after an earlier version of an upcoming Netflix documentary about the boxer featured her describing him as having “mild schizophrenia”. In a statement, she said she had used the term while recalling a conversation about Tyson’s mental health struggles several years ago, but acknowledged that it was not an accurate description of his medical history. “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” she said. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” She added that mental health was complex and that finding the right words to describe someone’s experiences was not always easy. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love,” she said. Paris also praised her husband for speaking openly about his struggles and thanked the public for supporting their family. Netflix confirmed that it had updated the documentary following the family’s clarification about Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis. “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch,” the streaming platform said. item.title: Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas
item.description: Italy has listed 14 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for work visas under its 2026–2028 immigration programme, offering employment opportunities to foreign workers across several sectors of its economy. Nigeria is among the African countries on the list, alongside Ghana, Senegal, Morocco, Egypt and 10 others. The programme forms part of Italy’s broader labour migration policy, which seeks to admit foreign workers to address labour shortages and meet the country’s employment needs. Under the programme, the Italian government has reserved 25,000 work permits annually for citizens of 38 designated countries, including the 14 African nations. The African countries named are: Algeria Ivory Coast Egypt Ethiopia The Gambia Ghana Mali Morocco Mauritius Niger Nigeria Senegal Sudan Tunisia. The employment opportunities cover sectors including agriculture, forestry, fishing, food production, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, tourism, transportation, logistics, healthcare and social assistance. According to the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the immigration programme provides for a total of 497,550 foreign workers to enter Italy between 2026 and 2028. The allocation is divided into 164,850 workers for 2026, 165,850 for 2027 and 166,850 for 2028. The figures cover seasonal and non-seasonal employment as well as self-employment. However, inclusion on the list does not automatically guarantee a work visa. Applicants must secure employment from an Italian employer, who is generally required to apply for the relevant work authorisation, known as nulla osta , before the worker proceeds with the visa application. For the 2026 allocation, applications for seasonal agricultural jobs were scheduled to open on January 12, while those for seasonal tourism jobs were scheduled for February 9. Applications for non-seasonal employment under the relevant categories were scheduled for February 16 and 18, 2026. The programme is part of Italy’s efforts to address labour shortages through regulated migration while strengthening cooperation with countries of origin. item.title: UK Reform leader vows to scrap Graduate visa route used by 20,478 Nigerians
item.description: UK Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, has vowed to scrap the United Kingdom’s Graduate visa route if his party wins power, a move that could affect thousands of Nigerians who use the scheme to remain in the country after completing their studies. Farage announced the proposal in a post on X on Thursday, arguing that the route allows foreign graduates to stay in the UK for two years after completing their degrees, competing with British workers for entry level jobs or potentially claiming asylum. Figures published by the UK Home Office on November 26 showed that 20,478 Nigerian nationals received grants under the Graduate route in the year to September 2026, making Nigerians the third largest group of beneficiaries. Indian nationals topped the list with 66,552 grants, followed by Pakistanis with 24,768. The three nationalities accounted for about 69 per cent of all grants recorded during the period. The Graduate route allows international students who have completed eligible courses at UK universities to remain in the country and work or look for employment without needing an immediate job offer or sponsorship. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has described the scheme as “a scam on the British people” and proposed replacing it with a 30 day period for graduates to secure a qualifying job that meets an economic value test. The party said about 800,000 Graduate visas, including those issued to dependants, had been granted since the route was introduced in July 2021. Yusuf also cited Home Office figures showing that 5,130 asylum claims were made by people who had previously held Graduate visas in the year to June 2026, twice the number recorded in the preceding year. The pledge comes as the Labour government is already preparing to reduce the standard duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months from January 1, 2027. The change will not apply to graduates from institutions that meet certain compliance and labour market outcome standards. However, Reform UK has yet to clarify how its proposed abolition would affect people who already hold Graduate visas or international students currently studying in the country. The latest Home Office figures also showed a decline in the number of Nigerian students receiving sponsored study visas. Grants to Nigerian nationals fell by 34 per cent to 19,734 in the year to September 2026, representing about six per cent of the total. item.title: Saudi Strike Kills 11 In Yemen
item.description: A Saudi strike killed 11 people on Friday in western Yemen, Houthi media said, a day after an attack by the Iran-backed movement on an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia. A Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government has been regularly bombing areas controlled by the armed group since the country’s civil war reignited over the summer. In response, Houthi forces have been targeting the oil-rich kingdom almost daily, hitting energy facilities, airports and the financial district of the capital, Riyadh. Saudi warplanes carried out a raid on a residential building in the city of Al-Turba in Taiz governorate on Friday, killing “11 citizens, most of them children,” the Houthis’ Saba news agency said, citing a local source. The agency also reported strikes targeting fuel tanks in the Saada region, the movement’s birthplace and stronghold. Smoke billows from the Yemeni capital Sanaa on November 26, 2026 after Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territories held by the Iran-backed group, hours after it struck Riyadh. Photo by AFP On Thursday, the Houthis targeted the Jazan refinery in southern Saudi Arabia, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several other people, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). The attack also triggered a fire that led to the shutdown of the facility, the SPA said. Yemen plunged back into war in July, after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the Middle East war. Hostilities intensified in September when the Houthis, who already controlled the most densely populated parts of Yemen, seized the western coastline overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait on the Red Sea. The Houthis are now advancing toward Aden, a major southern city where the government has taken refuge after being driven out of the capital Sanaa in 2015. Since the conflict resumed, fighting in Yemen has killed more than 2,300 people and displaced over 364,000, according to the United Nations. In Saudi Arabia, Houthi attacks have killed 27 people, according to the kingdom’s authorities. The post Saudi Strike Kills 11 In Yemen appeared first on Channels Television .

item.description: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, nearly 400 flights were cancelled, and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed. New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday due to what organisers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was cancelled for three years during World War II. Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds. item.title: 2027: Lokpobiri rallies Bayelsa West for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, has urged voters in Bayelsa West Senatorial District to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. Lokpobiri made the appeal on Thursday, November 26, during a pre-campaign sensitisation exercise organised by the Bayelsa West APC Campaign Directorate in Aleibiri, Ebedebiri and Agbere communities. Addressing party members, stakeholders and residents, the minister urged them to remain committed to the APC, saying sustained support for the party was necessary to consolidate the reforms and transformation being pursued by the Tinubu administration under its Renewed Hope Agenda. He said Tinubu had demonstrated the courage, vision and determination to reposition the country through what he described as bold reforms and purposeful leadership. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has remained committed to delivering on his Renewed Hope mandate and transforming our dear nation. The progress being made requires our collective support and commitment to ensure that the gains are sustained. We must therefore give him another mandate in 2027,” he said. The minister also called on the people to support all APC candidates, stressing that political unity, grassroots mobilisation and collective participation would be crucial to the party’s prospects in the elections. “I urge the good people of Bayelsa West to stand firmly with President Tinubu and all APC candidates. This is the time to consolidate our structures, strengthen our grassroots engagement and work together towards victory,” he added. The sensitisation exercise, according to the organisers, was part of the party’s efforts to strengthen grassroots mobilisation, encourage peaceful political participation and build support structures across Bayelsa West ahead of the 2027 general elections. He expressed concern that institutions established to fight corruption could be used to settle political scores, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. However, the allegations against Governor Yusuf remain claims by Kwankwaso and would require an independent response from the governor or his representatives. item.title: 2027: Emerging opposition coalition comprises displaced politicians — Lagos APC
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has criticised ongoing merger and coalition talks among opposition figures ahead of the 2027 general elections, describing the emerging alliance as an association of “internally displaced politicians” driven by personal grievances rather than a coherent vision for governance. The Lagos APC spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark on Friday, questioned the ideological consistency and sincerity of the political actors seeking to unite against President Bola Tinubu in 2027. According to Oladejo, the emerging alliance comprises former power brokers, ex-officeholders and frustrated aspirants who previously benefited from or helped shape the same political establishments they now criticise. He maintained that the coalition lacked a unified policy framework on critical national issues, including economic management, energy reforms, foreign exchange policy and national security. “What is being marketed to Nigerians as a formidable opposition coalition increasingly looks like an assembly of politically displaced persons, disgruntled power brokers, frustrated presidential aspirants and former beneficiaries of the very political establishments they now denounce,” the Lagos APC spokesman said. Reacting to another round of opposition consultations scheduled for Monday, Oladejo dismissed the repeated meetings as “political motion without movement”. He argued that bringing prominent political figures together under one roof did not automatically translate into grassroots electoral structures or administrative competence. Oladejo further contended that opposition rhetoric had become excessively focused on opposing Tinubu rather than presenting a credible alternative blueprint for governance. While acknowledging that the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had brought difficult adjustments for households and businesses, the Lagos APC maintained that the 2027 election would be determined by verifiable performance records, policy continuity and organisational strength rather than what it described as a “coalition of grievances”. item.title: Questions about Tinubu’s identity come up anytime he’s about to win election — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed renewed questions about President Bola Tinubu’s background and identity, saying the controversies resurface whenever the president is on the verge of winning an election. Fashola described the questions as needless distractions, insisting that Tinubu had met the constitutional requirements to contest the presidency and that Nigerians had already settled the matter through their votes. He said the controversy had persisted for more than two decades but had not stopped Tinubu from winning elections, expressing confidence that the president would secure another victory in 2027. Fashola spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to questions about the perceived secrecy surrounding Tinubu’s background and identity. “I think that these matters have carried on for all of 20-something years. So, every time he’s at the threshold of winning an election, these issues come, and you know what always happens: he wins,” he said. “So history is about to repeat itself again. He’s going to win. These are needless distractions. They don’t answer a fundamental question. And I’ve said about minimum qualification. He has met it,” the former governor added. Fashola questioned the relevance of the controversies to Nigerians, saying opposition politicians should focus on issues that would improve the lives of citizens rather than repeatedly raising questions about Tinubu’s background. “The question I will focus upon if I were those fragmented opposition is how does this help the people whose mandate I want? It doesn’t help them,” he said. The former minister of works also argued that some of the issues had previously been subjected to legal proceedings and investigations, including during the 1999 political period and the last presidential election. Drawing on his experience as a legal practitioner, Fashola said there was a need to allow an end to prolonged disputes, invoking the legal principle that litigation must eventually come to a conclusion. “I believe parts of this were litigated in the last election. They were litigated in 1999. It was the subject of a House investigation in that period. You keep referring to my other life as a legal practitioner, there’s a principle in that life. There’s something we say, a principle that there must be an end to litigation. It’s enough,” he said. Fashola said Nigerians had moved on from the controversy, citing Tinubu’s victory in the 2023 presidential election as evidence, and predicted that voters would reaffirm their position in 2027. “They pursue it at their own choice, but I think the Nigerian people have left that subject behind. They have left it behind with their votes in 2023. They will reaffirm it in 2027,” he said. Fashola said politicians who opposed Tinubu in the past had now joined forces with him, describing the president’s ability to bring former adversaries together as evidence of his leadership and capacity to work with others. He spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to why Nigerians should give Tinubu another four years in office. The former minister of works said voters should assess the presidential candidates based on their relationships with people they previously worked with, arguing that the ability to sustain working relationships through difficult periods was an important measure of leadership. “The three main presidential candidates today share one trait in common. They all started as governors. One of them didn’t take office, but he was already a governor-elect, Vice President Atiku Abubakar. Where are all the people who worked with them today?
